findings.title: Concurrency test never joins reader thread, so assertion can race
findings.body: The test starts a bare reader thread and then asserts `caughtExceptions` is empty immediately after setting `deletedAll`. There is no `join()` (nor a timeout) on the thread, so an exception thrown in the last iterations of the reader loop may be recorded after the assertion runs, making the test pass even when the regression is present. The thread is also never interrupted/stopped if the test fails early, leaking a thread that keeps hitting the admin API. Join the thread (with timeout) before asserting.

findings.title: Created groups are not registered for cleanup
findings.body: The 100 groups created in `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` are only removed by the explicit delete loop; if `fail()` or an exception occurs earlier (e.g. during creation or removal), the groups remain in the shared realm and can affect other tests in the class, which use the same injected realm. Register them via `managedRealm.cleanup()` as the other tests do.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount() can now return null, propagating null into representations
findings.body: `getSubGroupsCount()` returns `null` when the group has been removed concurrently (model supplier yields null). Callers such as `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` do `representation.setSubGroupCount(group.getSubGroupsCount())` without a null check, so a null subGroupCount is serialized/returned to clients, and any caller unboxing the Long will still NPE. Consider returning 0L, or handling the removed-group case explicitly (e.g. skipping the group) instead of leaking null through the GroupModel contract.
